tutorials.title: Interface tour
tutorials.description: Workflow tabs, sidebar, main area and status bar.

tutorials.title: Simulation
tutorials.description: Define a structure and calculate its pattern.

steps.title: Open Project
steps.text: Simulation. Your own project is put aside until the end of this tutorial. Click Start to begin on the Project page.

steps.title: New project
steps.text: Create a new project with Create a new project.
steps.expected: The Create project dialog is open.

steps.title: Name the project
steps.text: Give the project a name, for example lbco: type it in Name, or press Next.

steps.title: Create it
steps.text: Click OK to create the project. It is not saved: at the end you keep working on it or return to your own project.

steps.title: Open Structure
steps.text: This is the Structure page, where structures are defined. Open the Structure page with its tab, or press Next.

steps.title: New structure
steps.text: Create a structure.
steps.expected: A structure is in the list.

steps.title: Name it
steps.text: A new structure is called structure1. Click its name and type lbco, the name this tutorial uses from here on.

steps.title: Open Space group
steps.text: Open the Space group group to see the structure's symmetry.
steps.expected: The Space group group is open.

steps.title: Space group
steps.text: A new structure starts in P b n m. Choose the space group P m -3 m for lbco.
steps.expected: The space group is P m -3 m, number 221.

steps.title: Open Cell
steps.text: Open the Cell group to see the cell lengths and angles.

steps.title: Cell length
steps.text: Set the cell length a to 3.89 Å. In a cubic cell b and c follow it.
steps.expected: a, b and c are 3.89 Å.

steps.title: Open Atom sites
steps.text: Open the Atom sites group to see the structure's atoms.
steps.expected: The Atom sites group is open.

steps.title: Add the atoms
steps.text: A new structure has one atom site. Add three more, then set them: La at 0, 0, 0 and Ba on the same position, each with occupancy 0.5; Co at ½, ½, ½; O at 0, ½, ½.
steps.expected: The four atom sites are in the table and the structure view shows them.

steps.title: Open Experiment
steps.text: Open the Experiment page with its tab, or press Next.

steps.title: New experiment
steps.text: Open the Experiment page and create an experiment.
steps.expected: The new experiment is in the list.

steps.title: Experiment type
steps.text: Powder, constant wavelength and neutrons are selected by default. For your own data you can change them here; in this tutorial keep the defaults.
steps.expected: The experiment type is powder, constant wavelength, neutron.

steps.title: Open Instrument
steps.text: Open the Instrument group to see the wavelength and the zero shift.

steps.title: Wavelength
steps.text: A new experiment starts at 1 Å, because every experiment has its own wavelength. Set it to 1.494 Å, HRPT's, the one this tutorial uses.

steps.title: Open Linked structures
steps.text: Open the Linked structures group to see the structures in this pattern.
steps.expected: The Linked structures group is open.

steps.title: Scale
steps.text: Every structure is linked to a new experiment automatically, so lbco is here with scale 1. Here you can change a scale or weight fraction, switch a link off or add another.

steps.title: The pattern
steps.text: The calculated pattern of lbco is in the main area. Change the cell length or a position and watch the peaks move.
steps.expected: The main area shows the calculated pattern.

steps.title: Open Analysis
steps.text: Parameters can be changed on the Structure and Experiment pages, in their groups, and also here on the Analysis page, in one table that holds all of them. Open the Analysis page with its tab, or press Next.

steps.title: Show the cell
steps.text: The table holds every parameter; its filters find the one to change. Choose Cell in the category filter.
steps.expected: The table lists the cell length a.

steps.title: Select cell a
steps.text: Click the row of the cell length a to select it: the slider below the table now changes a.
steps.expected: The cell length a is selected.

steps.title: Change cell a
steps.text: Drag the slider or type a new value, and watch the peaks shift: a larger cell moves them to lower angles.
steps.expected: The cell length a has changed.

steps.title: Clear filters
steps.text: Clear the filters with the eraser.

steps.title: Filter by name
steps.text: Type wave in the name filter to show the wavelength.

steps.title: Select wavelength
steps.text: Click the row of the wavelength to select it: the slider below the table now changes the wavelength.

steps.title: Change wavelength
steps.text: Drag the slider or type a new value, and watch the peaks spread out to higher angles as it grows.

steps.title: Clear filters
steps.text: Clear the filters with the eraser.

steps.title: Show B iso
steps.text: Choose Atomic displacement in the category filter.
steps.expected: The table lists the sites' B_iso.

steps.title: Select B iso
steps.text: Click the row of La's B_iso to select it: the slider below the table now changes La's B_iso.

steps.title: Change B iso
steps.text: Drag the slider or type a new value, and watch the peaks at high angles weaken most as it grows.

steps.title: Clear filters
steps.text: Clear the filters with the eraser.

steps.title: Show the peak
steps.text: Choose Peak profile in the category filter.
steps.expected: The table lists the peak profile.

steps.title: Select peak width
steps.text: Click the row of the peak width W to select it: the slider below the table now changes W.
steps.expected: The peak width W is selected.

steps.title: Change peak width
steps.text: Drag the slider or type a new value, and watch the peaks broaden as it grows.
steps.expected: The peak width W has changed.

steps.title: Clear filters
steps.text: Clear the filters with the eraser.

steps.title: Free column
steps.text: With measured data, the free column is where fitting chooses the parameters it may change. A simulation has nothing to fit, so here they all stay fixed.
steps.expected: The free column is in the table.

steps.title: Open Report
steps.text: A simulation has a useful report too: lbco, the experiment and the calculated pattern. Open the Report page with its tab, or press Next.

steps.title: Open Export
steps.text: Open the Export group to see how the report is saved.

steps.title: Save the report
steps.text: Choose HTML, PDF or CIF and press Save to write the report. In this tutorial you may skip saving.

tutorials.title: Fitting
tutorials.description: Fit LBCO measured on HRPT, from a CIF and a data file.

steps.title: Open Project
steps.text: Fitting. Your own project is put aside until the end of this tutorial. Click Start to begin on the Project page.

steps.title: New project
steps.text: This tutorial builds a fitting project from a structure file and a measured pattern. Create a new project with Create a new project.
steps.expected: The Create project dialog is open.

steps.title: Name the project
steps.text: Give the project a name, for example lbco: type it in Name, or press Next.

steps.title: Create it
steps.text: Click OK to create the project. It is not saved: at the end you keep working on it or return to your own project.

steps.title: Save the files
steps.text: Save the tutorial's two files, lbco.cif and hrpt.xye, with Save tutorial files below and a folder of your choice, or press Next to save them to a temporary folder.

steps.title: Open Structure
steps.text: Open the Structure page with its tab, or press Next.

steps.title: Load the CIF
steps.text: On the Structure page, load the structure from lbco.cif: Load ▾, then From file….
steps.expected: The structure lbco is in the list.

steps.title: From the CIF
steps.text: lbco.cif gave the space group P m -3 m, the cell of 3.88 Å and four atom sites: La and Ba share one site, each half occupied.

steps.title: Open Experiment
steps.text: Open the Experiment page with its tab, or press Next.

steps.title: New experiment
steps.text: On the Experiment page, create an experiment.
steps.expected: The new experiment is in the list.

steps.title: Experiment type
steps.text: An .xye file holds only the pattern, so choose its kind first. Powder, constant wavelength and neutrons, as HRPT measures, are selected by default: keep them.
steps.expected: The experiment type is powder, constant wavelength, neutron.

steps.title: Load the data
steps.text: Load the measured pattern from hrpt.xye: Load ▾, then From file… under Measured data.
steps.expected: The measured pattern is in the main area.

steps.title: Open Instrument
steps.text: Open the Instrument group to see the wavelength and the zero shift.

steps.title: Wavelength
steps.text: A new experiment starts at 1 Å, because every experiment has its own wavelength. Set it to 1.494 Å, HRPT's.

steps.title: Zero shift
steps.text: Set the 2θ zero shift to 0.3°, where the fit starts.

steps.title: Open Peak profile
steps.text: Open the Peak profile group to see the peak shape.
steps.expected: The Peak profile group is open.

steps.title: Peak shape
steps.text: The Thompson-Cox-Hastings pseudo-Voigt is the default profile, and V and W keep their defaults, −0.1 and 0.1. Set U to 0.08 and Y to 0.08.

steps.title: Open Linked structures
steps.text: Open the Linked structures group to see lbco in the pattern.
steps.expected: The Linked structures group is open.

steps.title: Scale
steps.text: lbco was linked to the experiment by itself. Set its scale to 9, where the fit starts.

steps.title: Open Background
steps.text: Open the Background group to see the background points.

steps.title: Estimate background
steps.text: Estimate the background from the measured pattern.
steps.expected: The background points follow the bottom of the pattern.

steps.title: Name the points
steps.text: Name the points by their position with Id from position.
steps.expected: Each point is named by its position.

steps.title: Open Analysis
steps.text: Open the Analysis page with its tab, or press Next.

steps.title: Show the scale
steps.text: Fit in stages, a few parameters at a time, with the table's filters. First show only the scale: choose Linked structures in the category filter.

steps.title: Free the scale
steps.text: Open the menu of the free column's header and choose Free · all: it frees only the rows the filters show.

steps.title: Show background
steps.text: Now choose Background: the intensities of the background points.
steps.expected: The table lists the background points.

steps.title: Free the background
steps.text: Free the background points too. Open the menu of the free column's header and choose Free · all: it frees only the rows the filters show.

steps.title: Fit
steps.text: Start the fit.

steps.title: Fit results
steps.text: The fit's results: its status, the reduced chi-squared and the R values of each dataset. Close them with OK.

steps.title: Clear filters
steps.text: Clear the filters with the eraser before the next stage.

steps.title: Show the cell
steps.text: Next the cell: choose Cell. The cubic cell has one free length, a.
steps.expected: The table lists the cell length a.

steps.title: Free the cell
steps.text: Free the cell length. Open the menu of the free column's header and choose Free · all: it frees only the rows the filters show.
steps.expected: The cell length a is free.

steps.title: Clear filters
steps.text: Clear the filters with the eraser.

steps.title: Filter by name
steps.text: The zero shift is one of the instrument's two parameters: type offset in the name filter to show it alone.
steps.expected: The table lists the zero shift.

steps.title: Free the zero
steps.text: Free the zero shift. Open the menu of the free column's header and choose Free · all: it frees only the rows the filters show.

steps.title: Fit again
steps.text: Fit again, then close the results with OK.
steps.expected: The fit has finished and its results are closed.

steps.title: Clear filters
steps.text: Clear the filters with the eraser before the next stage.

steps.title: Show the peak
steps.text: Then the peak profile: choose Peak profile.
steps.expected: The table lists the peak profile.

steps.title: Free the peak
steps.text: Free the peak profile. Open the menu of the free column's header and choose Free · all: it frees only the rows the filters show.

steps.title: Fit again
steps.text: Fit again, then close the results with OK.
steps.expected: The fit has finished and its results are closed.

steps.title: Clear filters
steps.text: Clear the filters with the eraser before the next stage.

steps.title: Show B iso
steps.text: The symmetry of P m -3 m fixes every position, so the displacements are left: choose Atomic displacement.
steps.expected: The table lists the B_iso of the sites.

steps.title: Free the B iso
steps.text: Free every site's B_iso, La's and Ba's included. Open the menu of the free column's header and choose Free · all: it frees only the rows the filters show.

steps.title: Fit again
steps.text: Fit again, then close the results with OK.
steps.expected: The fit has finished and its results are closed.

steps.title: Uncertainties
steps.text: Look at the s.u. column: La's and Ba's B_iso have large uncertainties, because the pattern cannot tell the two halves of one site apart.
steps.expected: The uncertainties are in the table.

steps.title: Clear filters
steps.text: Clear the filters with the eraser.

steps.title: Correlations
steps.text: Open Correlations to see why.

steps.title: Correlated pair
steps.text: La's and Ba's B_iso are fully anticorrelated (−1.00): the fit only fixes them together. A constraint gives them one value.

steps.title: Extra tab
steps.text: Open the Extra tab.

steps.title: Open Aliases
steps.text: Open the Aliases group to name parameters for a constraint.

steps.title: Add aliases
steps.text: Add two aliases: biso_La for La's B_iso and biso_Ba for Ba's.
steps.expected: The two aliases are in the list.

steps.title: Open Constraints
steps.text: Open the Constraints group to tie the two values.

steps.title: Add a constraint
steps.text: Add a constraint and write biso_Ba = biso_La.
steps.expected: The constraint is in the list.

steps.title: Fit again
steps.text: Fit again, then close the results with OK: Ba's B_iso now follows La's, and the shared value has a small uncertainty.

steps.title: Correlations again
steps.text: Correlations again: the square of La's and Ba's B_iso is gone, since Ba's now follows La's.

steps.title: Fit quality
steps.text: The fit's quality on Pattern: the calculated pattern lies on the measured one, the residual below is flat, and the experiment's line gives Rwp and the reduced chi-squared.

steps.title: Your own work
steps.text: In your own work you would go on freeing or fixing parameters and fitting until the fit is good. This example fits well, so it stops here.
steps.expected: The fit is good and needs no more stages.

steps.title: Open Report
steps.text: The Report page summarises the fitted model: the structure, the experiment, the fit and its quality. Open the Report page with its tab, or press Next.

steps.title: Open Export
steps.text: Open the Export group to see how the report is saved.

steps.title: Save the report
steps.text: Choose HTML, PDF or CIF and press Save to write the report.

steps.title: Save the project
steps.text: Save the project with the save button in the app bar: the tutorial's project is not saved until you save it.
